credits_cram.why: Says "Hoover et al. (2026) introduced CRAM" and calls its own work "an independent, clean-room CPU re-implementation" of CRAM, so it is not claimed as new.

cites_hoover.why: The body text uses \citet{hoover2026classical} repeatedly, in the introduction, related work, methodology and results.

small_n.why: Limitations: "our direct LLM evaluation was restricted to a sample of 5 to 10 puzzles per model tier"; the setup section gives the same counts.

handset_caveat.why: Reports the hand-set energy solves 497/500, "identical" to the learned model's 496-497, and says this confirms Hoover et al.'s caution about Sudoku.

their_numbers.why: The 99.996% and 42 ms H200 figures are attributed to Hoover et al.; the authors' own runs are reported on an M4 Pro CPU at 2.5 s.

no_new_claims.why: Adds details absent from the log: 24 GB memory, clue range 22-28, Python 3.12, per-model synthesis times, Haiku max 182.4 s, and a hand-set peer recovery of 1.000.
